title: The innermost reliability zeros of complete graphs and Waldvogel's constant
description:
Unrefereed research candidate. Take a network in which every link fails independently with the same probability q. The all-terminal reliability polynomial R(q) is the chance that the network stays connected. For the complete graph Kn (every pair of n nodes linked) it is the probability that a random graph is connected. Because R is a polynomial, one can ask where it vanishes for complex q. These reliability zeros have been studied since the Brown–Colbourn conjecture that they all lie in the closed unit disk, which Royle and Sokal showed is false in general. Plots show the zeros of Kn creeping out towards the unit circle as n grows; Buys proved that Rn → 1 inside the disk and asked whether the zeros of graphs and matroids spread evenly round the circle.

Results. (1) The smallest modulus hn of a zero of Rn satisfies −n log hn = 2 log n − 2(1 + log W0) + o(1), where W0 = 0.7377507574… is the rotation-restricted Whittaker constant studied by Waldvogel in 1983; so the innermost zeros lie at distance about (2 log n − 1.392)/n inside the unit circle. (2) Interval arithmetic shows that the innermost zeros approach the two directions arg q = ±2.3932… (about ±137.1°), not the negative real axis, and gives hn to absolute error o(n−2). (3) On the arc π/30 ≤ arg q ≤ 59π/30, which asymptotically carries 29/30 of the zeros, a joint limit law for the angle and the rescaled distance to the circle, with an explicit profile. (4) For all sufficiently large n the negative real axis carries exactly one zero when n ≡ 0, 3 (mod 4) and none otherwise, located with error O(n−4); exact computation confirms the count for 2 ≤ n ≤ 24. (5) A short criterion based on the theorem of Hughes and Nikeghbali, answering a question of Buys: the zero-counting measures of the spanning reliability of loopless matroids converge to the uniform measure on the unit circle exactly when rank divided by size tends to zero.

Idea of the proof. The generating function for connected graphs is cut at half its length. A graph has at most one component with more than n/2 vertices, so the reliability splits exactly into a one-giant-component term close to 1 (Gilbert) and an only-small-components term governed by the smallest zero of the deformed exponential function (Sokal). A zero needs the two terms to cancel, which pins the radius; the closest approach occurs where that smallest zero is smallest, which is Waldvogel's constant.

Limits. The negative-axis count is proved for all sufficiently large n, with no explicit threshold, and checked exactly for 2 ≤ n ≤ 24. The limit law leaves out an arc of 1/30 of the circle near q = 1 and says nothing about a vanishing fraction of the zeros; whether every zero of Rn lies inside the unit circle is still open. The directions, the precise radius and the 29/30 arc rest on interval-arithmetic certificates.

Contents. The paper (LaTeX source and PDF), its two figures with data, ten Python programs (exact real-zero counts, the Whittaker/Waldvogel certificate with two independent interval backends, the arc certificates, high-precision finite-size checks, derived constants and the figures) and their recorded outputs. Certificate programs raise an error on any failed inequality, also under python -O. Also included: the bibliography, a machine-readable index, a research-gate record, a review summary, a replay receipt and SHA-256 sums.

Assurance. Written proofs with computer-assisted interval certificates. Internal AI-assisted review only: a combined five-perspective Claude review panel, one revision round with extensions, a re-review, a proof audit of the new and rewritten proofs, and clean replays with negative controls. No Astra/Codex review took place. This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Text CC0-1.0; code MIT.
